predecessors.name: Zhou dynasty
predecessors.text: Ji, the walled City of Ji (Jicheng) 'in the southwestern part of present-day Beijing', Guang'anmen area

successors.name: Yan (state)
successors.text: Ji, the walled City of Ji (Jicheng) 'in the southwestern part of present-day Beijing', Guang'anmen area

ledger.x: c. 1045: King Wu enfeoffs the ruler of Ji. In the 11th year of his reign King Wu 'deposed Di Xin and conferred titles to nobles within his domain', including the rulers of Ji and Yan; the page dates it about 1045 BC and calls it 'the first mention of Ji in history'.
7th century BC: the state of Ji ends in Yan's conquest; year not on the page.

wars.name: Yan conquest of Ji
wars.outcome: Yan conquered Ji in the 7th century BC and made the City of Ji its capital; the city stayed the main urban centre of the area until the 13th century.

certainty.note: No Ji boundary is on the page; soft throughout.
